title: No Measurable Benefit from Verifier‑Assisted Generate→Validate→Repair under Shared‑Initial Generation: A Preregistered Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and autonomously executed a paired emulation study (study‑cnd‑2026‑001) that tested whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline increases oracle pass rates for LLM‑produced network configurations on vendor‑diverse emulated NetOps intent→configuration tasks. The frozen design used paired evaluation (Npairs=200), generation semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one generated candidate consumed by both conditions), declared model gpt‑5‑mini, a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5), and a repair budget ≤1 call/task. Execution produced 200 complete pairs (400 episodes), model_calls_used=200, and repair calls invoked=0. Outcome: baseline = 200/200 oracle passes; guarded = 200/200 oracle passes; absolute paired difference = 0.00 (paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar two‑sided p=1.00). The null result is design‑bound: because a single shared candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle in every case, the guarded repair stage was never exercised. We release the full audited artifact bundle (preregistration, prompts, raw outputs, provider traces, validator traces, execution manifest and SHA‑256 digests) and interpret the run‑level null result as a ceiling effect caused by the preregistered shared generation semantics and high oracle coverage. We provide artifact‑anchored recommendations to obtain informative comparisons in future evaluations (independent sampling, calibrated task difficulty, larger repair budgets, and validator stress tests).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being explored as intent→configuration agents for NetOps. A key operational concern is misconfiguration risk: syntactically plausible but operationally incorrect configurations (ordering errors, vendor‑idiom mismatch, unsafe transitions) can cause outages or security violations. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→repair: a generator proposes an artifact, a deterministic validator (oracle) checks objective properties (reachability, ordering, protected interfaces), and a repair module iteratively fixes violations until the oracle accepts. Prior empirical reports and prototypes (constraint‑based adaptation, abstention, verifier‑assisted repair in other domains) suggest that verifier‑assistance may reduce failure rates, but quantitative evidence under preregistered, auditable conditions is limited. We preregistered a confirmatory paired experiment to measure whether a verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair pipeline improves oracle pass rates relative to unconstrained generation. The preregistration fixed the critical generation semantics: shared_initial_candidate (one generated candidate per pair, consumed by both baseline and guarded conditions). This choice is central to the observed outcome and is declared transparently in the preregistration artifact (see preregistration SHA‑256). The contributions are: an artifact‑anchored preregistered paired emulation run; a transparent account explaining why the guarded pipeline was not exercised in this run; and reproducible recommendations, grounded in the archived artifacts, for informative future evaluations.
sections.related_work: LLM‑assisted NetOps research spans intent translation, configuration synthesis, and verifier/constraint augmentation. Benchmarks and prototypes such as NetConfEval investigate translation accuracy; system proposals (LLM‑NetCFG, MeshAgent) demonstrate improved reliability when invariants and validators are encoded; verifier‑grounded repair workflows (e.g., StruSpec in program/DSL domains) show measurable improvements when execution + counterexamples drive localized repairs. Our work differs: we preregistered the experiment design and execution semantics, performed an auditable autonomous run that archived every prompt, response, provider trace and validator trace, and report a confirmatory null result that is traceable to the frozen generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate). Representative verified sources used for positioning include Zhou et al. (MeshAgent), Wang et al. (NetConfEval), and Ding (StruSpec); these records are archived and cited in our evidence bundle.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design: We preregistered study‑cnd‑2026‑001 (SHA‑256: a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Design: paired binary evaluation with Npairs=200 (400 episodes planned and executed). Task bank: four protocol buckets (BGP, OSPF, ACL, VLAN) of 50 pairs each; within each protocol the vendor allocation is Cisco=17, Juniper=17, Arista=16 (total Cisco=68, Juniper=68, Arista=64). Complexity: per protocol 25 simple and 25 complex tasks (total simple=100, complex=100). Model and adapter: declared model gpt‑5‑mini via hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Generation semantics (frozen): shared_initial_candidate — a single generator call per pair produced one candidate provided to both conditions. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (deterministic oracle implemented in the testbed). Repair policy: at most one repair call per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1). Analysis plan: paired_binary_analysis_v1; paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. Missingness policy: require complete pairs for primary analysis; provider/infrastructure failures are excluded and logged. Execution logging and artifact preservation: every prompt, model output, provider call trace, validator trace, and analysis artifact was archived and SHA‑256 hashed (execution/execution_manifest.json; representative hashes and paths are included in the artifact bundle).
sections.results: Execution summary (artifact‑backed): the run completed per the preregistered plan: planned_episode_count=400, completed_episode_count=400, failed_episode_count=0, model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per pair). Scoring: baseline_success_count=200/200 (100%), guarded_success_count=200/200 (100%); repair calls invoked=0. Primary confirmatory analysis: absolute paired difference = 0.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00] (bootstrap_resamples=10,000, seed=1729); McNemar two‑sided p=1.00. The paired contingency is fully concordant: n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; these values and the full contingency table are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 available). Representative per‑pair validator traces show the shared candidate, parsed commands, validator parse results, and validation outcome (example: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; SHA‑256 = eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b). Deterministic reconciliation (artifact: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) confirms accounting consistency across provider calls, raw responses, scoring files and analysis artifacts.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and causal account: the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced one generated candidate per pair that was consumed by both baseline and guarded scoring paths. In this run, every shared candidate passed the deterministic oracle; repair was therefore never invoked (repair_calls_invoked = 0). Consequently the guarded repair pipeline had no opportunity to act and the confirmatory paired comparison is uninformative about potential benefits of repair under independent sampling or harder failure conditions. This is a design‑bound null result, not falsification that verifier‑assistance can never improve reliability. Operational implications: evaluations of generate→validate→repair pipelines must ensure the experimental design permits the guarded pathway to be exercised. Artifact‑backed recommendations (directly executable from the archived bundle): (1) independent generation semantics — sample an independent candidate per condition per pair to measure generator variance and allow repair to act; (2) task difficulty calibration — increase oracle coverage variance by adding more adversarial or boundary tasks so that the generator produces some failing candidates; (3) repair budget and iterative repair — allow multiple repair iterations and richer repair prompts so the repair module can demonstrate improvement; (4) validator stress‑testing — vary validator strictness and include oracle coverage diagnostics to detect blind spots; (5) multi‑model replication — evaluate across multiple models to assess generality. Reproducibility: all artifacts (preregistration, model configuration, prompts, raw responses, provider traces, scoring records, analysis artifacts) are archived with SHA‑256 digests and file paths; key artifacts referenced in this paper include execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, execution/responses/, execution/scoring/, and analysis/* (see artifact hashes in the evidence bundle). Limitations and threats to validity (artifact‑grounded): the study is intentionally narrow — single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini), single deterministic validator, synthetic/emulated tasks, and frozen shared generation semantics. These constraints preserve internal reproducibility but limit external generalization.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed an auditable paired study that compared verifier‑assisted generate→validate→repair to unconstrained generation under a frozen design. Under the chosen shared_initial_candidate semantics and the provided emulated task bank, every shared generated candidate passed the deterministic oracle; repair was never invoked and both conditions achieved perfect oracle pass rates (200/200). The observed null result is therefore traceable to the preregistered generation semantics and high oracle coverage. We release the full artifact bundle and provide artifact‑anchored recommendations (independent sampling, calibrated task difficulty, larger repair budgets, and validator diagnostics) to produce informative future comparisons. The artifacts permit reproducible reruns and direct extension to independent‑generation or iterative‑repair variants, enabling the community to quantify the practical benefit of verifier‑assisted workflows under regimes where repair is exercised.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement (artifact‑backed):
- Initial master prompt reference (immutable archive): provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). This master prompt launched the autonomous post‑lock research run. The Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved the master prompt pre‑lock; all substantive research actions reported here were performed autonomously after the lock.
- Preregistration (frozen): study id = study-cnd-2026-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = a8969ac01f3b1bb7585872c58a92f72d0752160dd4e6e01cbafbfe0d15073ad2. The preregistration froze the primary hypothesis, sampling plan, generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate), declared model, validator, repair budget, stopping rules, and analysis executor.
- LLM and adapter: declared model = gpt-5-mini used via hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter; model configuration artifact: execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). All provider call traces and raw responses are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/responses/ with per‑file SHA‑256 digests recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json.
- Generation semantics (frozen): shared_initial_candidate (one generated candidate per pair and provided to both baseline and guarded conditions). This preregistered choice produced model_calls_used=200 (one shared generation per 200 pairs) and is the proximate cause the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0). The execution manifest records these counts and per‑file hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json).
- Validator and oracle: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored every candidate; representative scoring artifact: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 = eaf96aec12c30860a6fd70987289cc71104134a3330b99c7e024f244dbd35c1b). All validator traces are archived and hashed.
- Repair policy and budgeting: preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; in this run repair calls invoked = 0 (artifact‑backed). Repair prompts would have been archived if used.
- Analysis procedures (frozen): paired_binary_analysis_v1; paired bootstrap 10,000 resamples (seed=1729) and exact McNemar two‑sided test. Confirmatory analysis artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951).
- Execution and reproducibility: every prompt, model output, provider trace, validator trace, scoring file, manifest and analysis artifact is archived with SHA‑256 digests. Deterministic reconciliation confirms arithmetic and accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; SHA‑256 = 799b23b993fcc9c04fc4d0a375e975937bc11d9f8c6595d43dce94375411d174).
- Human involvement: pre‑lock collaborative development and approval of the master prompt were performed by the Research Director. No human performed manual substantive editing of the manuscript after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development artifacts were not used as empirical evidence unless reproduced under the frozen post‑lock workflow.
- Deviations: none affecting the primary confirmatory analysis; model identifier did not change mid‑run; no pairs excluded; repair stage not triggered. Full execution manifest and per‑file SHA‑256 digests are included in the artifact bundle for audit.
limitations: Confirmatory conclusions apply only to the exact preregistered design (shared_initial_candidate semantics, single declared model gpt‑5‑mini, deterministic_netops_validator_v5, synthetic/emulated task bank of 200).

Shared_initial_candidate execution semantics created a ceiling effect: because the single shared generated candidate per pair passed the deterministic oracle for every task, the guarded repair stage was never invoked (repair calls invoked = 0), preventing measurable guarded benefit in this run.
Emulation with a deterministic validator and synthetic tasks does not capture full production heterogeneity (real vendor images, runtime nondeterminism, device‑specific quirks).
Single‑model execution limits generality across model families and instruction‑tuning variants.
Repair budget was intentionally limited (≤1 call/task) by preregistration; richer iterative repair policies remain unexplored in this run.
Oracle blind spots (uncovered semantic failure modes) remain possible; oracle‑coverage diagnostics are archived and annotated in the artifact bundle.
